source_narratives.raw_material: 8 sources: a pitch deck, 3 sales call transcripts, the public marketing site, 2 competitor-alternatives pages, and a partnership announcement. Decks gave strong category-framing signal; transcripts revealed buyer committee shape.
source_narratives.primary_research: 3 competitor dossiers pulled from public sources. Strong category-shape signal — every named competitor sells to integrated health systems and anchors on transport reliability or outcomes.

folders.label: Strategy

framework_dispatches.why_first: Anchors downstream messaging and competitive framing

folders.summary: Strong working hypothesis that Marley competes against manual spreadsheet dispatch (Component 1), not against named SaaS — three converging sources support this. The lead-attribute question (real-time visibility vs automated re-routing) is open and forces a homepage tradeoff. Market-category framing is the weakest sub-area.
folders.provided_summary: 8 sources plus 3 competitor dossiers; no customer-voice interviews or win/loss calls.

input_asks.ask: The alternative each recent buyer almost chose instead of you (one line per buyer, from email, survey, or sales-call note)
What category name did your team or investors use when pitching the company last year?
Your three most recent win announcements — enough to infer the buyer type and use case without a formal case study

folders.label: Language
folders.summary: Tone signal converges across the marketing site and three sales decks — direct, outcome-first, low-jargon. The main open question is whether to anchor on 'operations' or 'logistics' as the primary category noun. Voice work is mature enough to move forward.
folders.provided_summary: Marketing site, 3 sales decks, and transcripts available; no formal brand-voice brief on file.

input_asks.ask: Three phrases your best customers use when describing the problem you solve — exact words from email, Slack, or survey responses
Any words or phrases the team has banned from sales decks or marketing copy, and why

folders.label: Audiences
folders.summary: Three payer segments classify confidently from source material: commercial, Medicaid, and Medicare Advantage. ACO and direct-to-consumer are flagged as low-confidence — one mention each, neither corroborated. The employer procurement channel dominates the sales motion; payer-direct is mentioned but unconfirmed.
folders.provided_summary: Sales transcripts and deal notes only; no direct buyer or user interviews from any segment.

input_asks.ask: List of your top 10 current customers with industry, company size, and which team owns the relationship
Any segment or vertical your team has explicitly ruled out as a target, and the reason

folders.label: Personas

framework_dispatches.why_first: Persona feeds messaging and sales pitch

folders.summary: Head of Operations is the dominant persona, surfaced across eight sales transcripts. CFO appears in deal mentions but the role profile is thin. The largest gap: no source material from the actual user (the dispatcher) — all signal comes from buyers above them, which risks a polished buyer story with a hollow user story.
folders.provided_summary: 8 buyer-side sales transcripts; no dispatcher interviews or end-user surveys.

input_asks.ask: The job title and department of the person who signed your last three contracts
The job title of whoever uses the product daily — if different from the buyer
One sentence each of what the buyer cares about vs. what the daily user cares about, in their own words if possible

folders.label: Market

framework_dispatches.why_first: Required by sales enablement and competitive context

folders.summary: DispatchTrack has the strongest evidence as a named competitor (positioning deck + two competitor pages). Roundtrip and Kaizen Health appear once each — likely watchlist rather than active competitive set. Behavioral alternatives (spreadsheets, in-house dispatcher, no formal routing) have stronger evidence than any named-competitor field.
folders.provided_summary: 3 competitor dossiers and 2 competitor-alternatives pages; no win/loss analysis or direct intel.

input_asks.ask: The competitors you put on your battle card — company name and the one-line reason you win against each
One deal you lost to a competitor in the last 6 months and what the buyer said was the deciding factor

folders.label: Proof

framework_dispatches.why_first: Validates claims before going to market

folders.summary: The weakest folder in this build. The headline '15-minute routing' stat has one source and no controlled benchmark. Compliance posture (HIPAA, SOC 2) is named but unsupported by evidence in the ingested set. Three P0 questions need answers before this folder can support sales conversations.
folders.provided_summary: One customer quote per headline metric; no case study PDFs, benchmarks, or compliance certifications.

input_asks.ask: The specific metric from your best customer result — number, what was measured, time period, and whether it was self-reported or independently verified

folders.label: Design
